rationale: Repair of the previous rejection (trial-4556240c94: quality passed, rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise/objective_not_improved with candidate medians 30.63/25.59 ms vs parent 24.94/25.13 ms). That attempt replaced the layer body with Triton elementwise kernels while keeping aten reductions/GEMMs/SDPA: GPU work was unchanged but ~300 extra Python-side Triton launches per prefill added host cost, so TTFT got worse. The collector evidence identifies the actual recoverable loss: the root prefill call c9d14173dd4887d4a4133553 executes 2145 kernels with cuda_us 21624.6 (GEMM 15.51 ms, elementwise 3.30 ms, lm_head gemv 0.83 ms, reduce 0.71 ms, cat 0.54 ms, flash 0.74 ms) while warm parent wall TTFT is 24.94-25.13 ms, i.e. ~3.3-3.5 ms per invocation is host launch gap (python_runtime confirms transformers forward self-time dominates the host; the decode loop shows the same CPU-bound effect at ~11.8 ms GPU busy vs ~21.8 ms wall per step). This candidate therefore removes launch overhead instead of replacing kernels: on the first graph-eligible invocation (inside the live adapter phase context, per the binding contract) it captures the CURRENT parent callable from context.references into a CUDA graph after side-stream warmup, validates one replay bitwise (logits plus every per-layer K/V tensor, torch.equal) against the eager parent run, and from then on copies the current input_ids into the static buffer and replays. The identical captured kernels, order and addresses execute on every invocation, so outputs are bitwise identical to eager (exact greedy tokens and the 0.02 logits tolerance hold by construction), the KV cache returned per replay is a fresh config-built DynamicCache wrapper over the static prefill K/V tensors (the eager decode loop and the teacher-forced quality run see exactly parent cache semantics), and nothing about the fixed fixture is precomputed: only kernel work is captured, inputs are copied in and all math re-executes per invocation. Decode-step calls and every other signature/shape fall back to the parent behind labeled guards (context/signature/setup/validation/runtime), and any failure permanently reverts to the parent, so a broken graph costs the gain, never quality. Expected replay wall is GPU busy (~21.6 ms) plus small replay/copy/argmax overhead, a ~2.5-3.5 ms TTFT gain, above the observed per-pair noise bounds (2.05/0.77 ms).
setup_work: Lazy, one-time, entirely inside the first graph-eligible invocation (quality phase, untimed; never inside a timed repeat): (1) one eager parent prefill whose result is returned as that invocation's output; (2) two parent warmup iterations on a side stream with the static input buffer; (3) one torch.cuda.graph capture of the parent forward on that stream (capture context performs torch.cuda.synchronize and empty_cache internally); (4) one validation replay plus bitwise compares (logits and 36 per-layer key/value tensors). Retained after setup for the worker lifetime: the CUDAGraph and its private memory pool holding the prefill activation working set and the static output tensors (input_ids 4 KiB, last-token logits ~0.3 MiB, prefill K/V ~37.7 MiB, plus pool-resident intermediates on the order of the eager prefill activation footprint), and the graph object itself. Memory-counter expectations: per-invocation peak_allocated_bytes may fall for replay invocations because prefill intermediates are allocated once in the retained graph pool during setup rather than per run; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include the capture and the retained pool, and reserved_bytes grows by the pool. No counter decrease is claimed as a physical memory saving; the objective is ttft_ms only.
quality_risks: Replay must be bitwise identical to the eager parent; this is enforced once at capture time (torch.equal on logits and every per-layer K/V tensor) and any mismatch permanently routes to the parent with the parent_fallback_validation label, so quality cannot fail from a numerical divergence (the risk inherited from trial-e262267559 cannot recur: no kernels are rewritten).

Capture can fail on unsupported ops or allocator/stream conditions; such failures are caught, labeled parent_fallback_setup_failure, and the bundle degrades permanently to the parent (no gain, correct output).

Decode steps, non-(1,256)-shaped prompts, extra kwargs, enabled autograd, or an outer stream capture fall back to the parent by signature/context guards (labels parent_fallback_signature / parent_fallback_context); the decode loop is untouched.

Coverage: the declared replacement is a Python callable invoked on every call at the boundary (replay or fallback), and replay genuinely re-executes the captured native kernels each invocation on freshly copied inputs; CUDA Graph replay does not rerun the parent's inner Python ops, which is exactly the eliminated host overhead, and no installed bundle (requires/replaces are empty) inherits functional calls inside this region.

Alias/state: each replay returns a fresh DynamicCache wrapper over static K/V tensors, so no mutable cache object is shared across invocations; within an invocation the harness's decode appends via torch.cat as with a parent cache. Graph-pool tensors are only read by the eager decode.

The first invocation is slower (~4 extra prefill executions for warmup/capture/validation); it lands in the untimed quality/warmup phase, and measurement boundaries, thresholds, workload and sampling semantics are unchanged.
